body_html:
Quick Answer: Missed Weekly GLP-1 Injection Rules: General prescribing instructions for a missed dose are within 5 days for Ozempic, within 4 days (96 hours) for Mounjaro and Zepbound, and for Wegovy only if your next scheduled shot is more than 48 hours away. If that window passed, skip it and resume on your regular day, and do not double dose. Always confirm with your pen's Medication Guide or pharmacist.

Once-weekly GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 medications are designed to stay active across the week, which makes them easier to manage than daily pills until travel, busy weekends, or pharmacy delays cause you to forget a shot.

Because each brand has slightly different prescribing instructions for grace windows and minimum spacing between injections, guessing can leave you under-dosed or increase nausea and side effects from overlapping doses. Use the comparison table below as a quick reference, and check your medication leaflet or ask your prescriber if you are unsure.

1. Why You Should Not Double Up on a Weekly GLP-1 Shot

Weekly GLP-1 medications are absorbed slowly after injection and remain active in the body for days. Injecting two doses within 48 hours stacks overlapping drug levels, increasing the risk of severe vomiting, dehydration, kidney strain, and low blood sugar (especially if paired with insulin or sulfonylureas).

If you miss the cutoff window (for example, you notice on Day 6 that you forgot Ozempic), skip that week and wait for your next scheduled day. Skipping a single late dose is generally safer than stacking two doses close together, and your next scheduled shot gets you back on track. Talk to a doctor or pharmacist if you miss multiple doses.

2. How to Safely Shift Your Weekly Injection Day

Many people intentionally shift their GLP-1 injection day schedule (for instance, switching from Monday morning to Friday evening so mild post-shot fatigue happens over the weekend). Standard prescribing instructions generally allow changing your injection day as long as you keep the minimum buffer between shots:

  1. Semaglutide (Ozempic / Wegovy): Wait at least 48 hours (2 full days) after your previous injection before taking a dose on your new preferred day.
  2. Tirzepatide (Mounjaro / Zepbound) & Dulaglutide (Trulicity): Wait at least 72 hours (3 full days) between consecutive injections.
  3. Reset Your Recurring Schedule: Once you inject on the new day, that weekday becomes your new weekly anchor going forward.

3. Four Habits to Remember a Once-a-Week Shot

Daily supplements like evening magnesium can become part of a bedtime routine. Because a once-weekly injection only happens every seventh day, standard calendar alerts are easy to swipe away and forget:

  • Anchor to a Weekend Ritual: Tie your injection to a regular weekly cue, such as Saturday morning coffee or Sunday meal prep, rather than a rushed weekday commute.
  • Log Your Injection Site: Rotating weekly between abdomen, thigh, and upper arm helps prevent skin irritation or firm tissue lumps that can affect absorption. Record the site in your dose note.
  • Log Every Shot as Taken: A generic calendar alert only tells you a dose was due. A dedicated weekly medication reminder app keeps a dose history, so on Day 4 or 5 you can check whether you actually injected instead of guessing (the same idea behind our missed pill guide).
  • Set Refill Warnings 5 Days Early: Many missed shots happen because of prior-authorization delays or pharmacy backorders. Track pen counts so refill alerts fire while one pen remains in the fridge.

4. A Simple Decision Checklist for a Missed Weekly Shot

When you realize a shot is late, answer three questions in order before you inject:

  1. Which drug is it? The window depends on the label: 5 days for Ozempic, 4 days for Mounjaro and Zepbound, the 48-hour rule for Wegovy, and 72 hours for Trulicity.
  2. When is my next scheduled dose? Count the hours, not just the days. A shot taken on Saturday night and the next one on Monday morning is less than 48 hours apart.
  3. Have I missed more than one week? After two or more missed weeks, call your prescriber before restarting, because they may adjust the dose to limit nausea.

Write down the date and time of the late shot so you can see the spacing next week, and ask your pharmacist or prescriber if you are unsure. For other dose-timing questions, see the full Pill Reminder guides library, or the Pill Reminder app page for how weekly and every-other-week schedules work.

faqs.question: What happens if I take my weekly semaglutide shot a day late?
faqs.answer: For most people, taking a shot one day late falls within the standard missed-dose window for weekly GLP-1 medications: within 5 days for Ozempic, and for Wegovy as long as your next dose is more than 48 hours away. Take it as soon as you remember, then go back to your usual day or keep the new day, as long as two doses are at least 48 hours apart.

faqs.question: What if I forget my weekly GLP-1 semaglutide injection for 5 or 6 days?
faqs.answer: For Ozempic, if more than 5 days have passed since your missed dose, skip it and take your next dose on your regularly scheduled day. For Wegovy, skip the missed dose if your next scheduled injection is 48 hours or less away. Do not take two doses within 48 hours, and ask your pharmacist or prescriber if you are unsure.

faqs.question: Can I change my GLP-1 injection day without skipping a week?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can usually change your weekly injection day as long as you maintain at least 48 hours (2 days) between doses for Ozempic or Wegovy, or at least 72 hours (3 days) between doses for Mounjaro, Zepbound, or Trulicity.

faqs.question: How do I remember a once-a-week injection without missing doses?
faqs.answer: Pair your shot with a consistent weekly anchor (like Sunday morning breakfast) and use a dedicated weekly medication reminder app with persistent snooze alerts and pen-count refill tracking so you are less likely to swipe away a notification before injecting.
